title: Visual Anything tour file
description: The contents of a `.vatour` file: a tour, steps that each take the canvas to a view state and explain it with a caption, played full screen to walk someone through a concept (ADR 0058).

steps.description: The steps in order. A step that names something deleted is kept, and played without it.

conflicts.description: What a merge could not join, as data (ADR 0072): each conflict says which item it is about, what the file keeps in place, and the other choice. Written only by a merge; the person resolves them.

Id.description: An identifier, generated once and never reused. Files refer to each other only by id. Element and relation ids share one namespace, because a relation can end on either. Component and relation type ids start with their package's id, as in `systems.service`.

viewState.description: Where the step takes the canvas and how it reads there; everything but its view is optional.

caption.description: What the caption card says while the step shows.

marks.description: The elements and relations the step highlights, as guidance highlights them. Left out when it highlights none.

play.description: A scenario played while the step shows, over the step's view.

reveal.description: Marks brought in one press forward at a time, after the step's own marks (ADR 0077).

dimRest.description: Dims everything the step does not mark, but the ends of the relations it marks.

advance.description: Moves on by itself; left out, the step waits for the person.

transition.description: `cut` makes the step always cut with a cross-fade (ADR 0084); left out, the shapes it shares with the step before glide to their new places when it can.

pulse.description: A marker sent along a chain of relations once the step's transition is over (ADR 0084).

notes.description: What the person presenting reads while the step shows, in the speaker notes window only: plain text, as a caption's.

TourStep.description: One step of a tour: where it takes the canvas, what it says there, and what it marks.

view.description: The view open on the canvas.

camera.description: Where the canvas looks; left out, the canvas shows the selection, or else the whole view.

select.description: What is selected: elements, relations and free shapes.

focus.description: Focus mode; left out, it is off.

scenario.description: The scenario open in the scenario panel, which plays over this view.

step.description: The step of that scenario playback is on, by its id; it needs `scenario`.

choices.description: The alternatives chosen at that scenario's decisions (ADR 0078); it needs `scenario`.

space.description: The physical-space panel, open beside the canvas (ADR 0076); left out, it is closed.

simulation.description: One simulation shown at one tick (ADR 0085); left out, none.

SavedViewState.description: A view state as a project file keeps it (ADR 0030's addendum): the view and, each optional, where the canvas looks, what is selected, the filters, focus mode, and the scenario open and its step. Everything is named by id, so that renames do not break it.

zoom.description: How large one canvas unit shows, in screen pixels.

SavedCamera.description: Where the canvas looks: the point of the view at its middle, in canvas units, and the zoom.

range.description: The time range what stays shown must meet (ADR 0025's clarification of W37).

SavedFilters.description: What a view state's filters hide: the elements created from some components, the relations of some relation types, whatever does not meet some conditions, and what falls outside a time range.

value.description: What the value is compared with; left out for `set` and `unset`.

SavedCondition.description: A condition on an attribute that elements, or relations, must meet to stay shown.

attribute.description: The attribute of the point, or of the start of a period.

until.description: The attribute of the end of a period, when the range is on periods.

kind.description: What the values read as: numbers, dates and date-times (milliseconds since 1970, UTC), or times of day (seconds since midnight).

from.description: One end of the range, on that axis; both are included, whichever way round.

to.description: The other end of the range.

SavedTimeRange.description: A time range of a view state's filters: what has a value for it outside the range is hidden, and what has none stays shown.

degrees.description: How many relations away it reaches, or every degree.

isolate.description: Whether it hides what it does not reach, instead of drawing it faintly.

from.description: The elements and relations it starts from; left out, it starts from the selection.

SavedFocus.description: Focus mode: how far it reaches, which way, whether it isolates, and what it starts from.

FocusDegrees.description: How many relations away focus reaches.

propertyNames.description: An identifier, generated once and never reused. Files refer to each other only by id. Element and relation ids share one namespace, because a relation can end on either. Component and relation type ids start with their package's id, as in `systems.service`.

DecisionChoices.description: The alternative chosen at each decision of a scenario, by the decision's id (ADR 0078). Choices belong to the tab that plays; a file keeps them only to play a given alternative from a tour's step or a view state.

root.description: The panel's root: World when left out, or one element.

camera.description: Where it looks; left out, it fits what it draws.

explode.description: How far each part moves away from the middle of what holds it: 0, the default, to 2.

relations.description: Whether the selection's relations are drawn in space; left out, they are not.

names.description: Whether names are written for the parts nearest the camera; left out, they are not.

joints.description: Joints' positions the panel shows, by joint, over their own (ADR 0090): degrees for a joint that turns, meters for one that slides. A tour's step moves the chain to them, gliding from the step before. Reading it changes nothing in the project.

SavedSpace.description: The physical-space panel in a view state (ADR 0076); its presence means the panel is open. Reading it changes nothing in the project.

target.description: The point it turns around, in the root's coordinates, in meters.

elevation.description: Degrees above the horizon, or below it when negative.

SpaceCamera.description: Where the physical-space panel looks: around a point, from a direction, at a distance.

SpaceTarget.description: A point in the root's coordinates that the physical-space panel looks at, in meters.

at.description: Where the plane crosses the axis, in meters.

keep.description: The side kept: the one below the plane along its axis, or above.

SpaceCut.description: A cutting plane across one of the root's axes, keeping one side of it.

JointPositions.description: Positions of joints by their ids.

JointPosition.description: A joint's position: degrees for a joint that turns, meters for one that slides, within the bound every joint's position keeps (the core's `MAX_JOINT_POSITION`).

parameters.description: The parameters chosen, by name; those left out keep their defaults.

seed.description: The run's seed; 1 when left out.

tick.description: The tick shown; 0 when left out.

SavedSimulation.description: One simulation a view state shows (ADR 0085): the element simulating, the parameters it chose, the seed and the tick shown. Reading it changes nothing in the project.

ParameterValue.description: A parameter's value: a number, a boolean, or one of its choices.

ParameterChoice.description: One of a choice parameter's choices.

place.description: The corner the card sits in; left out, the side of the screen farthest from the step's marks.

pointTo.description: One of the step's marks that a leader line from the card points at (ADR 0084): an element, a relation, a note or an arrow.

TourCaption.description: What a step's caption card says: a title and a text. Both are plain text, never HTML: a blank line starts a paragraph, and lines that start with "- ", or with a number and ". ", make a list.

from.description: The step it starts on; its first step when left out.

to.description: The step it stops on; its last step when left out.

choices.description: The alternatives it plays at the scenario's decisions; their defaults when left out.

TourPlayback.description: A scenario a step plays, from one of its steps to another.

text.description: Added to the caption as a paragraph when it comes in: plain text, as a caption's.

TourReveal.description: A part of a step's marks that comes in on its own press forward, with a sentence for the caption.

TourAdvance.description: When a step moves on by itself: after a number of milliseconds, never fewer than its caption takes to read, or `after-scenario`, once the scenario it plays ends.

AdvanceAfter.description: Milliseconds a step shows before it moves on by itself.

relations.description: The chain, in order: each relation shares an end with the next.

repeat.description: How many times it runs; left out, once.

TourPulse.description: A pulse (ADR 0084): a marker travels along each relation of a chain in turn, to show what follows what within one step.

item.description: The item, by a key local to its file: `world`, `element:<id>`, `relation:<id>` or `order` in the model file; `package`, `component:<id>`, `relation-type:<id>` or `image:<id>` in a package file; `view`, `position:<element>`, `position:<element> in <container>`, `free-shape:<id>`, `stacking:<container>` or `route:<relation>` in a view file; `scenario`, `step:<id>`, `tour`, `tour-step:<id>`, `thread` or `comment:<id>` in theirs; `project` in the project file.

path.description: Where the value lies inside the item, as a list of keys; empty for the whole item.

kept.description: Whose value the file holds in place.

other.description: The other side's value; left out when that side removed the item.

base.description: The common ancestor's value; left out when it had none.

sides.description: The names git gave the two sides, when it gave them.

FileConflict.description: What a merge of one project file could not join (ADR 0072). The file in place is a valid file of its kind; `other` and `base` are JSON as that kind of file holds the item, checked only when chosen.

ConflictReason.description: Why a merge could not join: both sides changed a value differently; one removed what the other changed; both added an id with different values; a removal meets what needs what it removes; two additions close a containment cycle; or both sides reordered a list differently.

ConflictSides.description: The names of a merge's two sides, as git gave them.
